===Etymology 1===
{{PIE word|en|tréyes}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*peh₂ǵ-}}
{{rfc|en|Middle Scots comes after Middle English.}}
From {{inh|en|enm|travelen|t=to make a laborious journey, travel}} from {{der|en|gmw-msc|travailen|t=to toil, work, travel}}, alteration of {{cog|enm|travaillen|t=to toil, work}}, from {{der|en|fro|travailler|t=to trouble, suffer, be worn out}}. See the {{glossary|doublet}}s {{doublet|en|travail|travois|notext=1}}.

Compare typologically {{m|en|routine}} << {{m+|la|rupta via}}. Note the inverse semantic vectors: ''travel'' moves from a subjective state (toil) to an objective action (journey), while ''routine'' moves from an objective object (beaten path) to a subjective pattern (habit).

Largely displaced native {{m|en|fare}}, from {{cog|ang|faran|t=to go [a long distance], to travel}}. More at {{m|en|fare}}.

# {{lb|en|physical}} A solid object in the shape of a circle.
## {{senseid|en|Q45926}}A [[circumscribing]] [[object]], (roughly) [[circular]] and [[hollow]], looking like an [[annual ring]], [[earring]], [[finger ring]] etc.
##: {{syn|en|annulus|hoop|torus}}
## {{senseid|en|Q46847}}{{lb|en|jewelry}} A [[round]] piece of ([[precious]]) [[metal]] [[worn]] around the [[finger]] or through the ear, nose, etc.
##: {{ux|en| His brother gifted him a '''ring''' for the engagement.}}
##* {{RQ:Shakespeare Merchant of Venice|IV|i|passage=The dearest '''ring''' in Venice will I give you.}}
## {{lb|en|UK}} A [[bird]] [[band#Noun|band]], a [[round]] piece of [[metal]] put around a [[bird]]'s [[leg]] used for identification and studies of [[migration]].
## {{senseid|en|burner-of-stove-etc}} {{lb|en|UK}} A [[burner#English:_burner-of-stove-etc|burner]] on a kitchen [[stove#Noun|stove]], [[hob#Noun|hob]]{{,}} or [[cooktop#Noun|cooktop]].
## A piece of [[food]] in the shape of a ring.
##: {{coi|en|onion '''rings'''}};   {{coi|en|calamari '''rings'''}}
## In a [[jack]] [[plug]], the connector between the [[tip]] and the [[sleeve]].
## {{lb|en|vulgar}} The rectum, anus, or anal sphincters.
##: {{ux|en|Lick my '''ring'''!}}
## {{lb|en|historical}} An [[instrument]], formerly used for taking the sun's [[altitude]], consisting of a brass ring suspended by a [[swivel]], with a hole at one side through which a solar ray entering indicated the altitude on the graduated inner surface opposite.
## {{lb|en|botany}} A flexible [[band]] partly or wholly encircling the [[spore]] [[case]]s of [[fern]]s.
# {{lb|en|physical}} A group of objects arranged in a circle.
## A circular group of people or objects.
##: {{ux|en|a '''ring''' of mushrooms growing in the wood}}
##* {{RQ:Milton Poems|poem=Il Penseroso|page=39|text=And hears the Muſes in a '''ring''', / Ay round about ''Joves'' Altar ſing.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1944|author={{w|Cecil Street|Miles Burton}}| title=[https://openlibrary.org/works/OL10563347W The Three Corpse Trick]| chapter=5| passage=The hovel stood in the centre of what had once been a vegetable garden, but was now a patch of rank weeds. Surrounding this, almost like a zareba, was an irregular '''ring''' of gorse and brambles, an unclaimed vestige of the original common.}}
## {{lb|en|astronomy}} A formation of various pieces of material orbiting around a [[planet]] or young [[star]].
##* {{quote-journal|en|journal=w:National Geographic|year=1990|month=August|volume=178|number=2|title=Neptune: Voyager's Last Picture Show|author=Rick Gore|page=40
|text=Soon Voyager will cross through the plane of Neptune's '''rings'''. This dusty, debris-laden zone is the most perilous passage. Most of the '''ring''' dust is the size of cigarette-smoke particles.}}
## {{lb|en|British}} A large circular [[prehistoric]] stone construction such as {{w|Stonehenge}}.
# {{senseid|en|encircling-contrastive-stripe}} A long [[stripe]] of [[contrastive]] material, colour, etc, that [[encircle]]s something.
#: {{ux|en|a '''ring''' of grime around the bathtub}}
# {{lb|en|internet}} {{ellipsis of|en|webring}}.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2002|author=Feroz Khan|title=Information Society in Global Age|page=100
|passage=Individuals looking to add their own homepage to a particular '''ring''' are, however, more or less at the mercy of the ringmaster, who often maintains a '''ring''' homepage listing its acceptance (or membership) policies and an index of its member sites.}}
# A place where some [[sports]] or [[exhibition]]s take place; notably a circular or comparable [[arena]], such as a [[boxing ring]] or a [[circus ring]]; hence the [[field]] of a political [[contest]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1707|author={{w|Edmund Smith (poet)|Edmund Smith}}|title=Phaedra and Hippolitus
|passage=Place me, O, place me in the dusty '''ring''', / Where youthful charioteers contend for glory.}}
#* {{quote-av|en|title=Meet the Soldier|role=Soldier|actor=w:Rick May|date=2009-01-19|time=0:14|publisher=w:Valve Corporation|location=Bellevue, Washington|network=YouTube|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250202131539/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h42d0WHRSck
|text=“If fighting is sure to result in victory, then you must fight!” Sun Tzu said that, and I'd say he knows a little more about fighting than you do, pal, because he invented it, and then he perfected it so that no living man could best him in the '''ring''' of honor.}}
## The open space in front of a [[racecourse]] [[stand]], used for betting purposes.
# {{senseid|en|illegal_group}} An [[exclusive]] [[group]] of people, usually involving some unethical or illegal practices. {{C|en|Corruption}}
#: {{ux|en|a crime '''ring'''; a prostitution '''ring'''; a bidding '''ring''' (at an auction sale)}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1877|author=w:Edward Augustus Freeman|title=The History of the Norman Conquest of England
|passage=the ruling '''ring''' at Constantinople}}
#* {{RQ:Sinclair Boston|passage=It's a blackmail '''ring''', and the district attorneys get a share of the loot.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=31 July 2018|author=Julia Carrie Wong| title=What is QAnon? Explaining the bizarre rightwing conspiracy theory| url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2018/jul/30/qanon-4chan-rightwing-conspiracy-theory-explained-trump| text=In a thread called “Calm Before the Storm”, and in subsequent posts, Q established his legend as a government insider with top security clearance who knew the truth about a secret struggle for power involving Donald Trump, the “deep state”, Robert Mueller, the Clintons, pedophile '''rings''', and other stuff.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013064304/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2018/jul/30/qanon-4chan-rightwing-conspiracy-theory-explained-trump|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
# {{lb|en|chemistry}} A group of [[atom]]s linked by [[bond]]s to form a closed [[chain]] in a [[molecule]].
#: {{ux|en|a benzene '''ring'''}}
# {{lb|en|geometry}} A [[planar]] [[geometrical]] [[figure]] included between two [[concentric]] [[circle]]s.
# {{lb|en|typography}} A [[diacritical mark]] in the shape of a [[hollow]] circle placed above or under the letter; a [[kroužek]].
# <!--Verify etymology, please-->{{lb|en|historical}} An old English [[measure]] of [[corn]] equal to the [[coomb]] or half a [[quarter]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1866|author=James Edwin Thorold Rogers|title=A History of Agriculture and Prices in England|volume=1|page=168
|passage=The '''ring''' is common in the Huntingdonshire accounts of Ramsey Abbey. It was equal to half a quarter, i.e., is identical with the coomb of the eastern counties}}
# {{lb|en|computing theory}} A [[hierarchical]] level of [[privilege]] in a computer system, usually at [[hardware]] level, used to protect data and functionality (also ''protection ring'').
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2007|author=Steve Anson; Steve Bunting|title=Mastering Windows Network Forensics and Investigation|page=70
|passage=Kernel Mode processes run in '''ring''' 0, and User Mode processes run in '''ring''' 3.}}
# {{lb|en|firearms}} Either of the pair of clamps used to hold a telescopic sight to a rifle.
# {{lb|en|cartomancy}} The twenty-fifth [[Lenormand]] card.
# {{lb|en|networking}} A [[network topology]] where [[connected]] [[device]]s form a [[circular]] [[data]] [[channel]]. All computers on the ring can see every message, and there are no [[collision]]s, and a [[single point of failure]] will occur if any part of the ring breaks.
# {{lb|en|slang|UK}} {{clipping of|en|ringpiece}}

===Etymology 1===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*terh₁-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|throwen}}, {{m|enm|thrawen}}, from {{inh|en|ang|þrāwan|t=to turn, twist}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*þrāan}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*þrēaną|t=to twist, turn}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*terh₁-|t=to rub, rub by twisting, twist, turn}}.

Cognate with {{cog|sco|thraw|t=to twist, turn, throw}}, {{cog|fy|triuwe|t=to push}}, {{cog|nl|draaien|t=to turn}}, {{cog|nds|draien}}, {{m|nds|dreien|t=to turn (in a lathe)}}, {{cog|de|drehen|t=to turn}}.

{{displaced|en|sl=1|warp}} as the word for hurling and was {{displaced|en|nocap=1|sl=1|by=1|warp}} as the word for twisting.

The use in computing comes from the fact, that in programming languages a statement reporting an error interrupts normal processing and sends an error object up the function calling stack until a handling statement intercepts it. Thus an “object” is “thrown” and “flies” until it is “caught”.

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:hore}}
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|hore}}, from {{inh|en|ang|hōre}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*hōrǭ}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*kéh₂ros|t=loved}}, from {{m|ine-pro|*keh₂-|t=to wish; desire}}. Cognate with {{cog|nl|hoer}}, {{cog|de|Hure}}, {{cog|non|hóra}} as well as {{cog|sa|चारु|tr=cā́ru||dear}}, {{cog|la|cārus||dear, expensive}}, and {{cog|ga|cara||friend}}. 

The unetymological spelling with ''wh-'' superficially denotes a formerly standard pronunciation with an excrescent {{IPAchar|/w/}} (such as in {{m|en|whole}}), but such a form is hardly found in either commentators on Early Modern English pronunciations or records of traditional dialects (which both explicitly mention its rarity or absence), therefore leaving the spelling somewhat inexplicable.<ref name="Dobson">{{R:en:Dobson:1957|II|430|998}}</ref> However, this may be because such an excrescent {{IPAchar|/w/}} was absorbed by a following {{IPAchar|/uː/}} (as in words with etymological {{IPAchar|/w/}} such as {{m|en|whom}}, {{m|en|two}}) after it became established in the spelling but before our earliest orthoepic records.

====Usage notes====
* The second meaning of {{m|en|refute||to deny the truth of}} is [[proscribed]] as [[erroneous]] by some [http://books.google.co.uk/books?id=2yJusP0vrdgC&pg=PA807&lpg=PA807&dq=english+usage+refute&source=web&ots=nYrYodyZZ4&sig=G_alFFyWi7ZFBMYnaujrrrh9qUM&hl=en&sa=X&oi=book_result&resnum=4&ct=result| (compare Merriam Webster,1994)]. An alternative term with such a meaning is {{m|en|repudiate}}, which means to reject or refuse to acknowledge, but without the implication of justification.
* ''Refute'' is also often confused with ''[[rebut]]''; a ''[[rebuttal]]'', in formal debate terms, is a counter-refutation, and it also has a specific legal sense, though like ''[[refutation]]'', the word has taken on the informal and disputed meaning of ''[[denial]]''.

Other linguists suggested that ''bull dyke(r)'' referred to strong black women who dug dikes, or derived from {{m|en|bull}} + {{m|en|dick}}, perhaps in reference to black men.Charles Panati, ''Sexy Origins and Intimate Things'' (1998), p. 181: "In fact, “bulldiking” is one of the earliest phrases in which the term “dike" has tough female overtones.
